chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sale of grape juice from one who makes it haram. He said: 'There is no objection to it; you sell it as halal, and they make it haram, so may God distance them and crush them.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection / It is permissible
key_terms.يَجْعَلُهُ حَرَاماً: Makes it haram (referring to the buyer's intent to ferment it into wine)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell grape juice to someone who will make wine from it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of *salamah al-'aqd* (validity of the contract) by distinguishing between the seller's act of selling and the buyer's subsequent use. He rules that the sale of grape juice is valid (*halal*) regardless of the buyer's intent to ferment it into wine, as the prohibition lies with the consumer, not the transaction itself. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that the intrinsic nature of the commodity determines the validity of the sale, while the buyer's intent determines the moral or legal status of its consumption.
